$comment: Deliberate, named deltas between a vendored copy and its canonical upstream. Keyed by the sync guard's title, then the vendored file name. Each record is (why, sha256 of the exact body it excuses): scripts/vendor_drift.py forgives that body and no other, and fails the job the moment upstream carries the change and the record is no longer true. tests/test_nest_pipeline_vendor.py holds every record to the in-repo pin. A record is a claim about the tree, dated and hashed, never a blanket permission — and it is the third thing a re-sync removes, after the body and the pin.

secrets.py.why: Word-boundary evasion hardening (80344b7, f35ab9d, 2026-09-11): every credential shape now matches on its own structure with no \b anchor, so a key glued to adjacent letters is still caught, and the AWS shape has no trailing anchor so same-charset glue cannot hide it. safe-app-store libs/nest-pipeline still carries the anchored shapes; re-syncing from it would revert the fix and turn tests/test_nest_secrets.py red. Upstream it, then remove this record.
